reading.body:
CyrusOne's Aurora campus publishes 114 megawatts of IT capacity, the largest disclosed figure in Illinois and 48 percent of the state's total, but only six of the state's 44 mapped facilities disclose power at all.

That gap is the real finding. Illinois has 44 mapped data center facilities and six with published power figures, so the state's visible capacity measures disclosure as much as it measures construction. One campus holding 48 percent of the disclosed total means the disclosed total is thin enough that a single operator's decision to publish dominates it.

The physical numbers describe a conventional hyperscale colocation build. At 450,000 square feet and 114 megawatts, the campus runs about 6.3 megawatts per 10,000 square feet. At 40 kilowatts per rack, a common AI training density, 114 megawatts translates to roughly 2,850 racks. The published specifications say nothing about power delivery tier, redundancy topology, cooling technology, or cooling source, so whether the building can sustain that density is not established by the disclosure.

For AI scaling the binding question is whether a campus can draw and cool its rated power, and on that the record is empty. CyrusOne publishes no total campus draw, no PUE, no renewable sourcing, no grid connection characteristics, and no cloud interconnect. Green Globes certification is the only environmental fact disclosed. The suitability score of 80 rests on published IT capacity and operator type alone, with announced expansion listed as missing. The campus is large by the only measure available and unverified on every measure that would decide whether it can serve training workloads.
